analysis: The overnight theme is beats getting punished. Apple posted a record September quarter ($114.5B, +12%) and Palantir nearly doubled revenue (+96%), yet both fell in premarket/after-hours trading — Apple on a December gross-margin guide of 45-46% as memory costs keep rising, Palantir on total contract value up only 6% after +49% in Q2. The market is no longer rewarding the print; it is charging for what the print implies about costs and future bookings. That is the same AI-spending skepticism that drove Monday's session: the Nasdaq-100 closed more than 10% below its all-time high, confirming a correction, while the Dow rose 0.41% and 8 of 11 sectors advanced — a rotation out of tech, not a broad selloff (equal-weight S&P rose 0.76% while the cap-weighted index fell 0.51%). What changed versus Monday's briefs: the morning rebound that held into late morning on Monday fully reversed in the afternoon, the VIX spiked back above 21 into the close, and oil's ~8% Monday slide partially reversed overnight on the Qeshm Island strike and a downbeat Iranian readout on a deal. Signal vs noise: the Apple margin story is signal — management called memory pricing unprecedented and rising beyond December, and it links directly to the chip tape (Nvidia bouncing 1.6% premarket after four down sessions, AMD +2.8% into its after-bell print). The midterm/prediction-market chatter is noise until results land overnight; the JOLTS and factory-orders prints today are the scheduled macro checkpoints. USAC is the brief's own catalyst: Q3 lands before the open with the call at 11 a.m. ET.
disclaimer: Not financial advice — for informational purposes only.

headlines.headline: Futures mixed on midterm election day: at 5:06 a.m. ET, Dow E-minis down 219 points (-0.42%), S&P 500 E-minis up 1.5 points (+0.02%), Nasdaq 100 E-minis up 130.5 points (+0.46%) (Reuters).
headlines.why_it_matters: A split tape into an election count — no broad risk-on or risk-off signal, so single-stock earnings are doing the steering.

headlines.headline: Apple beat then fell: fiscal Q4 revenue $114.5B (+12% YoY) vs $113.39B expected, EPS $2.10 vs $1.99 expected, iPhone $57.58B vs ~$56.5B expected; but December-quarter gross margin guided to 45-46% vs 47.9% in September, on memory costs CEO John Ternus called 'unprecedented' and rising beyond December. Shares fell ~4.5% in premarket trading (Reuters).
headlines.why_it_matters: The guide, not the beat, is the trade — margin compression from AI-driven memory scarcity hits the world's largest company and the whole device chain.

headlines.headline: Palantir fell despite a near-doubling: Q3 revenue $2.313B (+96% YoY) vs ~$2.18B expected, adjusted EPS $0.44 vs $0.41, full-year guidance raised to $8.53B; but total contract value rose only 6% YoY to $2.92B after +49% in Q2, and U.S. commercial contract value rose just 11% after +153% in Q2. Shares fell ~3% after hours, then ~6.3% in premarket per Reuters.
headlines.why_it_matters: Bookings decelerated sharply while revenue accelerated — the market is questioning how durable the growth is at a stretched valuation.

headlines.headline: Nasdaq-100 confirmed a correction: it closed Monday more than 10% below its all-time closing high after falling 1.07% on the day (Nasdaq Composite -1.07% to 25,164.32; S&P 500 -0.51% to 7,541.40; Dow +0.41% to 51,983.98) (Reuters).
headlines.why_it_matters: The correction label formalizes the AI-spending unwind — rallies now need to prove they hold, as Monday's early rebound faded by the close.

headlines.headline: Chips bounced premarket after leading Monday's selloff: Nvidia climbed 1.6% after four straight down sessions, AMD gained 2.8% ahead of its after-bell earnings, and Marvell and Intel moved higher (Reuters). Monday's damage: Intel -8.80%, AMD -7.52%, Micron -5.78%, Oracle -8.76% on its $20B raise.
headlines.why_it_matters: A relief bounce in the most beaten-down group — but after a correction close, it reads as stabilization, not a reversal, until AMD's print lands.

headlines.headline: Oil rebounded after Monday's slide: Brent +0.96% to $105.78 and WTI +1.08% to $97.50 in premarket, after reports the U.S. struck Iran's Qeshm Island and an Iranian official said a deal to end the war was far off (TipRanks/Reuters). Monday's session had seen crude fall ~8% on diplomacy hopes.
headlines.why_it_matters: The prior session's biggest tailwind is partially reversing — higher crude re-tightens the inflation headwind that helped Monday's early rebound.

headlines.headline: Midterms today: voters decide control of Congress; polls and analysts favor Democrats taking the House while Senate control remains uncertain. September JOLTs job openings and factory orders are also due today.
headlines.why_it_matters: Results emerge overnight, so traders carry election risk with no scheduled announcement to trade against — a reason futures are treading water.

headlines.headline: Anthropic reported a twelvefold increase in quarterly revenue and outlined plans to invest more than $895 billion over the coming years (Mitrade summary of overnight reports).
headlines.why_it_matters: Single-source, unconfirmed in detail — if the spending scale holds, it extends the AI-capex debate that is already pressuring tech; treat the $895B figure as fragile until a primary source confirms it.

usac.why_it_matters: No fresh USAC company news overnight. Q3 results are due before the open today with the call at 11 a.m. ET (company Oct 15 release); MarketBeat consensus is $0.3345 EPS on $348.32M revenue (Seeking Alpha preview: $0.37 on $348.06M). Units fell ~2.7% Monday to ~$24.80 per a MarketBeat snapshot, after closing Friday at $25.49 (+1.27%). The $0.525 Q3 distribution ($2.10 annualized) pays Nov 6 to holders of record Oct 26. Last reported quarter (Q2, Aug 4): EPS $0.31 beat the $0.28 consensus, revenue $342.15M vs $340.49M expected. Note: some aggregators list Nov 4 as the estimated date, but the company's own release schedules the release before today's open. Oil's overnight rebound after Monday's slide is a softer-to-firmer energy tape into the print, though USAC's business is natural-gas compression, not crude.
